info.title: Shodh a Code - contest platform backend
info.description:
Backend for **Shodh a Code**, a coding contest platform with an asynchronous judge.

Authentication
    Bearer tokens. The seed prints one per identity (see `evidence/seed-manifest.json` or the
    output of `make seed`). `POST /auth/dev/token` mints a token for any identity; it is a
    development fixture and is refused when `DEV_AUTH_ENABLED=false`.

Three credential scopes
    `user` participants and organizers, pinned to one organization
    `judge` the worker plane under `/internal/judge/*`
    `platform_admin` bootstrap of organizations and identities

Error shape
    Every failure is `{"error": {"type", "code", "message", "details", "request_id"}}`, where
    `type` is one of `validation` (422), `business_rule` (409), `authentication` (401),
    `authorization` (403), `not_found` (404) or `infrastructure` (503). A cross-tenant read is
    a 404 by design: knowing an identifier must not confirm that it exists.

Correlation
    Send `X-Request-Id` and it is echoed, stored on the submission, carried into the worker and
    printed in every structured log line for the operation.

post.description:
Deterministic fault injection for the recovery scenarios.

Refused unless the development authentication fixture is enabled, so a production build
cannot be told to break itself. The switch is stored in the database, so it reaches every
API process within one refresh interval rather than only the one that served this request.

post.summary: Submit a program (participant). Idempotent on Idempotency-Key.
post.description:
Idempotency

The key may be sent as the `Idempotency-Key` header or as `idempotency_key` in the body; if
both are present they must agree. The key is scoped to (contest, actor), so two participants
can use the same key safely and a key cannot be replayed into another contest.

A replay returns 200 with the original submission. Reusing the key with different code, a
different problem or a different language returns 409.

200.description: Replay: this key already created a submission

409.description: Key reused with different code or parameters, or a contest rule rejected it

get.summary: Standings, with a selectable computation path
get.description:
How clients observe updates

The response carries `standings_version`, a counter bumped inside the transaction that
stores a verdict, and an `ETag` identifying this representation: the version together with
the source, limit and offset, so paging with `If-None-Match` cannot be answered with a page
the client has never seen. A 304 means this exact page is unchanged. There is no
asynchronous refresh anywhere in the write path, so a successful read is never behind a
verdict that has already been stored.

`source` selects the computation path and exists for evidence, not for tuning:
  standings  the maintained problem_scores cells (what everyone gets by default)
  naive      recompute from submissions and attempts on every request (pre-optimization)
  rebuild    full recompute in Python from authoritative records
All three must return the same ranking; /standings/verify asserts it. The two re-deriving
paths are organizer-only, because they cost far more than the serving path.

get.summary: Assert that the serving path, the naive path and a full rebuild agree (organizer)

schema.title: Response Explain Standings Contests  Contest Id  Standings Explain Get

post.description:
Claims up to `capacity` jobs with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED.

Two workers calling this at the same instant cannot receive the same job: the row lock is
held in the database, not in any process. Each lease carries a `lease_epoch` that must be
presented with the result; the epoch is bumped on every lease and on every reclaim, so a
stale worker is fenced out.

get.summary: Re-read the judging payload for a held lease (judge scope)
get.description: Lets a worker that restarted mid-job recover its input without a new delivery.

schema.title: Response Payload Internal Judge Attempts  Attempt Id  Payload Get
Response Heartbeat Internal Judge Attempts  Attempt Id  Heartbeat Post

post.summary: Report a judging result (judge scope). Idempotent at a fixed lease epoch.
post.description:
What this call does, in one transaction

stores the per-test outcomes, derives the verdict, moves the attempt to COMPLETED, retires
the queue row, re-derives the submission status, and recomputes the one standings cell the
verdict can affect. Either all of that is visible or none of it is.

Replaying the same call with the same `lease_epoch` after a lost acknowledgement returns the
stored attempt and changes nothing.

409.description: Stale lease epoch, or the attempt is already finished

post.summary: Report that the judge could not judge (judge scope)
post.description:
Requeues within the delivery budget, otherwise marks the attempt INFRA_FAILED.

Neither path writes a verdict or touches a score: a runner crash or an unavailable service
is never a student error.

schema.title: Response Infra Failure Internal Judge Attempts  Attempt Id  Infra Failure Post

post.description: The API also does this on a timer; this route makes it deterministic in tests.
